data: Jupiter's gravity sculpted the asteroid belt — preventing a fifth rocky planet. Without it, Mars would be far larger.
Rotates in just 10 hours despite its enormous size, creating powerful magnetic fields. More massive than all other planets combined.
Pioneer 10 + 11 — NASA, 1973 / 1974 (first flybys; first close-up images)
Voyager 1 + 2 — NASA, 1979 (volcanism on Io, ring discovery, fine atmospheric detail)
Galileo — NASA, 1995–2003 (first Jupiter orbiter; atmospheric entry probe; Europa + Ganymede + Callisto + Io detail)
Cassini-Huygens — NASA / ESA / ASI, 2000 (gravity-assist flyby, joint imaging campaign with Galileo)
New Horizons — NASA, 2007 (gravity-assist flyby en route to Pluto; high-res Io and Europa)
Juno — NASA, 2016– (polar orbiter; magnetic field, JunoCam, deep atmospheric structure)
Europa Clipper — NASA, 2024– (en route to Jovian system; Europa close flybys from 2030)
JUICE — ESA, 2023– (en route; orbital insertion at Ganymede in 2034)
Jupiter has 101 confirmed moons — the four Galileans (Io, Europa, Ganymede, Callisto) are each worlds in their own right and trace a 1:2:4 orbital resonance.
Jupiter's magnetosphere is the largest planetary structure in the solar system — extending past Saturn's orbit on the anti-sunward side.
Jupiter is the favoured gravity-assist target for outer-system missions — Voyager 1+2, Cassini, Galileo, New Horizons, Juno, Europa Clipper and JUICE all used or use a Jovian flyby for velocity gain.
Jupiter's vast Hill sphere (50 million km radius) is what makes its 101-moon system stable — the gravitational well extends nearly to Mars at perihelion.
Juno (NASA) is currently in polar orbit; Europa Clipper (NASA) and JUICE (ESA) are en route — orbital arrival at Ganymede 2034.
Galileo's four-night observation in 1610 ended geocentrism. The system's moons are still ending old assumptions today.
Every planet's magnetosphere is different. Saturn's is uniquely aligned, Uranus's is chaotic, Venus and Mars don't have one at all.
Steal a planet's orbital momentum on a flyby — the closest thing in space to a free lunch.
The volume of space where a planet's gravity wins out over the Sun's.
What's at each planet right now: from MRO at Mars to Juno at Jupiter — while Venus has had no orbiter since Akatsuki ended in 2025.
